- **Dispatch ≠ success** — handing an event to the publish pipeline is not the same as it landing. Rust owns a **local publish intent / status fact** (pending → signed → stored → planned → sent → failed/exhausted), so the app gets honest, offline-first write state instead of optimistic fire-and-forget. [...] **4. A local publish intent is created immediately — before anything touches the network.**
The first thing the kernel does is mint a **status fact** owned by Rust: `pending`. This is the offline-first root — the write exists and is durable *before* a signer or relay is involved. This is why "dispatch ≠ success": the app gets a real status object, not a fire-and-forget. [...] - **A write is a tracked object with a lifecycle, not a function call.** The whole point of the write-door redesign is that "I published a note" is a durable, observable status fact that survives offline and reports honest terminal outcomes — versus the old model where dispatching and succeeding were conflated.
